purpose: Diagnose whether the opposite apparent treatment effects reflect writer behavior, judge preferences, or both; not search for a favorable evaluator.

motivation.pointwise_limit: No original untreated article was rated salient; the original cohort does not demonstrate slop elimination.

selection: Every original full-versus-bare pair and every corresponding single article, regardless of previous opinion or schema validity. Compact is not part of this primary-contrast diagnostic.
presentation: Reuse each exact original judge prompt, including unchanged A/B orientation and evidence IDs. Only the judging model changes; the runtime date wrapper is separately captured.

analysis_rules: Retain all requests, raw opinions, receipts and failures; do not retry until a preferred result appears.
Keep the original strict-parser verdict and a separate pointwise prefix-normalization verdict.
Pointwise normalization may only map pNNN to an existing text-pNNN; no decision or reason changes.
Report both judges, disagreement and all four writer/judge cells, not only the more favorable evaluator.
Report missing assessments and matched-pair coverage before agreement calculations.
Repeated writers, judges, variants and observations do not increase the twelve reporting-packet families.
No p-value, powered efficacy, human reader validation or default promotion from this diagnostic.
limitations: New judges share a model family with the writer; they may favor familiar prose.
Fresh isolated sessions prevent shared conversation, not common training or stylistic preferences.
Single judgments include stochastic variation; this is not a clean decomposition of every cause of disagreement.
The fixed fictional corpus and two model families do not represent all writing tasks or human editors.
